summary: Find records whose optional value is missing.
syntax: SELECT columns FROM table_name WHERE optional_column IS NULL;
documentation: IS NULL tests whether an expression has the SQL NULL value. Unlike equality comparison with NULL, this produces a useful true-or-false condition.
inputs: An expression that may be NULL.
returns: A condition suitable for filtering rows.
caution: An empty string is a value, not NULL. Comparing a column with = NULL does not select its NULL rows.
scenarios: Find orders missing a customer association.
Review contacts without an optional field.
Detect incomplete imports before a follow-up step.
title: Find orders without a customer
problem: Return id from orders where customer IS NULL, ordered by id ascending. Do not treat an empty string as missing.
goal: Use IS NULL or an equivalent approach that demonstrates the same concept.
hint: Filter with IS NULL, then order by id.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT query against the example tables.
SELECT 1;

tests.name: Missing and named
tests.setup: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer TEXT, amount_cents INTEGER, status TEXT); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (2, NULL, 100, 'paid'), (1, 'Micki', 200, 'paid'), (3, NULL, 300, 'paid');

tests.name: Empty is present
tests.setup: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer TEXT, amount_cents INTEGER, status TEXT); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, '', 100, 'paid');
